To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary supplementation with trans-18 :1 (trans-11 + trans-12) isomers (6 g/d for 6 weeks) did not affect biomarkers of inflammation or immune function.
dietary supplementation of trans-fatty acids (trans-11-and trans-12- 18 : 1; 6·0 g trans-18 :1/d) did not affect biomarkers of inflammation, immune function and adipose tissue function in humans.

dietary supplementation with trans-18 :1 isomers (6 g/d for 6 weeks) had no effect on inflammatory or immune biomarkers in healthy subjects, but increased the levels of these isomers and the endogenously synthesised cis-9,trans-11-CLA in leucocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of single trans-18 :1 isomers (i.e. trans-11- or trans-12- 18:1) on immune function, inflammatory biomarkers, and immune cell fatty acids in humans.
the effects of trans-fatty acids on immune cell fatty acid composition and immune function.
the impact of dietary supplementation with two trans-fatty acids on biomarkers of immunological function and inflammation in human immune cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trans-fatty acid supplementation does not affect biomarkers of inflammation, but the effects of single trans isomers are largely unknown and should be further investigated.
the effects of trans-11 and trans 12-18:1 on immune function and inflammation is unclear.
the dietary supplementation of vaccenic acid and trans-12 C18 : 1 had no effect on the biomarkers of inflammation, but the endogenous synthesis of trans-11 CLA from vaccenic acid was demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trans-isomer supplementation does not affect biomarkers of inflammation or immune function.
trans-11 and trans12 18:1 isomers do not affect biomarkers of inflammation or immune function in healthy humans, but they do increase cis9, trans11-CLA in immune cells.
the supplementation with trans-fatty acids did not affect the biomarkers of inflammation or immune function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trans-11- (and to a lesser extent trans-12-) 18 : 1 supplementation does not affect immune cells or biomarkers of inflammation.
the trans-isomers of vaccenic acid are converted to CLA in human cells and that the trans-11-iso-mer of vaccenic acid is the main precursor for CLA in human immune cells.
trans-isomers are not equivalent to one another.
